title: Recipe 54 — `tool-codegraph` (AST-aware code navigation as a tool)

beats.label: Open the recipe
beats.cue: “Grep finds strings. A code graph finds callers, definitions, and references — and the agent stops guessing.”

beats.label: Start from a blank spec
beats.cue: live/ is scratch — nothing committed is touched by a take.

beats.label: Load the API key
beats.cue: [needs-key] Sources demos/.env for the run beat.

groups.title: Beat 1 · wiring it into a spec

beats.label: Type the recipe's spec
beats.cue: “A crew, because navigation and editing are different jobs — and only one of them needs the graph.”

beats.label: Lint it
beats.cue: “The graph-crew well-formedness pass runs here — a role nobody routes to is caught before you pay for it.”

beats.label: Show the lowered IR
beats.cue: “The codegraph tool is an ordinary tool in the IR. Nothing downstream treats it specially.”

beats.label: Open the IR
beats.cue: “Which means permissions, justification gates, and audit all apply to it for free.”

beats.label: Compile the bundle — and check it
beats.cue: “--check: GREEN, gated at the model credential.”

verify.note: GREEN — assertion ok; install ok; boot gated at the provider credentials gate

beats.label: Type the factory injection
beats.cue: “_injectCodeGraphFactory — the seam for swapping the backing index without touching a spec.”

beats.label: Prove it parses
beats.cue: “Real TypeScript from the recipe — a file you can keep, not an illustration.”
beats.command: bun -e 'const s = require("fs").readFileSync("live/inject.ts","utf8"); new Bun.Transpiler({ loader: "ts" }).transformSync(s); console.log("live/inject.ts: parses as TypeScript");'

verify.note: the recipe's injection fence is syntactically valid TS

beats.label: Open it
beats.cue: “Underscore-prefixed, because it's a test and integration seam — not the public surface.”

groups.title: One more thing · point it at a real repo

beats.label: Install the graph package
beats.cue: [manual] “The recipe's Installing step — a third-party package, added to your project, not vendored by the compiler.”

verify.note: mutates package.json; a human decides whether to take the dependency

beats.label: Run it against this repo
beats.cue: [needs-key] “Ask it something grep would get wrong — 'who calls this?' — and watch it answer from the graph.”

verify.note: needs the codegraph package installed and a model credential

beats.label: Ask a navigation question
beats.cue: [needs-key] “A string search would return every mention. The graph returns the callers.”
beats.text: Who calls runChatLoop, and what do they pass for tools?
